title: Cheese Enchiladas
subtitle: Corn tortillas filled with cheese and onion, baked in a red chilli sauce
excerpt: Corn tortillas filled with grated cheese and finely chopped onion, rolled and baked under a smoky red chilli sauce, then finished with more cheese. The simplest enchilada, and one of the best.
sourceNotes: Cheese enchiladas: a classic Tex-Mex vegetarian enchilada, popular across the American Southwest. Often served as a side to beef enchiladas or as a meatless main. Based on classic Tex-Mex home-cooking tradition of the American border states.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble and freeze before baking for up to 3 months. Bake from frozen, adding 15 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze one tray unbaked.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead, cover, and refrigerate. Bring to room temperature before baking.

content.text: Cheese enchiladas are the simplest and most reliable enchilada to make: corn tortillas filled with grated cheddar and raw onion, rolled, and baked under a red chilli sauce until the filling melts into the tortilla. The raw onion inside softens as it bakes and gives a sharp contrast to the cheese. No pre-cooking of the filling; the oven does the work.

items.prepNote: soaked in boiling water 20 minutes, drained, seeds removed

content.text: Use a high-melting cheese like cheddar; low-moisture cheeses melt cleanly rather than going greasy. Grate it finely so it melts through the filling as well as the top.

Blend the drained soaked anchos, tinned tomatoes, garlic, and cumin until smooth. Pour into a medium saucepan with {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon. Season with salt.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Spread a ladleful of red sauce across the base of a roasting dish.
Dip each corn tortilla into the warm sauce for 10 seconds. Lay flat and fill with 2 tablespoons of grated cheese and a spoonful of chopped onion. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the dish.

Pour the remaining sauce over the enchiladas. Scatter the rest of the cheese on top. Bake at 190°C for 20-25 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are beginning to brown. Rest 5 minutes, then top with soured cream and sliced spring onion.

items.symptom: Cheese inside is oily and separated
items.cause: Cheese overheated, or a high-fat cheese used
items.fix: Cheddar works best. Keep the oven at 190°C and don't overbake; 20-25 minutes is enough for the cheese to melt without separating.
Chop the onion as finely as possible; very fine onion cooks through in the 25-minute bake. Coarser pieces stay sharp.

items.cause: Not dipped in the warm sauce
items.fix: The sauce dip is essential for corn tortillas; they crack without it. Keep the sauce at a low simmer while you work.

items.symptom: Dish is too dry after baking
items.cause: Too little sauce on top, or sauce reduced too far before assembly
items.fix: Use enough sauce to cover the enchiladas in a thin, even layer before baking. The sauce thickens as it bakes, so slightly thin before assembly is correct.

content.text: Cheese enchiladas are a mainstay of Tex-Mex cooking, served as a side dish alongside beans and rice or as a simple main on their own. In Texas, they are often served with chilli gravy (a beef-enriched chilli sauce) rather than the tomato-based red sauce used here. Both versions follow the same principle: cheese filling, corn tortilla, sauce, bake, eat hot.
